## Passages
RESULT [agents]: Found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices (the first improvement over Strassen for that case in 56 years), and a scheduling heuristic that recovers on average 0.7% of Google's fleet-wide compute. Stated limitation: 'it handles problems for which it is possible to devise an automated evaluator.'
US [agents]: Its limitation is the key lesson: autonomy scales only as far as a trusted automated evaluator reaches. For us the evaluator is the leak-free, correctly species-mapped holdout scorer, so its correctness comes before any autonomy. The evaluation cascade (cheap label-sanity and near-dup checks, then a short-schedule gate, then the full gate) cuts cluster cost per increment.
CORRECTION [agents]: 48 scalar multiplications for 4x4 complex matrices (first improvement over Strassen in 56 years), 0.7% fleet-wide compute recovered, evaluation-cascade quote, evaluator h, and limitation quote all confirmed.
